items.t: Toyota Surges Post Q2 Earnings: Is the Stock Worth Buying Now?
sum: Toyota TM shares rose more than 9% yesterday following its second-quarter fiscal 2027 results, taking its monthly gains to roughly 20%, outperforming the industry and its peers Honda HMC and Nissan NSANY. While Honda shares gained 14.5% over the past month, Nissan stock fell roughly 2%.

The rally may appear surprising at first glance, considering the automaker reported an 18.5% year-over-year decline in net income to ¥759.4 billion in second-quarter fiscal 2027. However, investors focused on two more encouraging developments — a stronger full-year profit outlook and an expanded shareholder-return program.

Toyota's latest results suggest that its operating business is performing better than its bottom line indicates. Meanwhile, its hybrid-focused strategy, improving North American profitability and higher shareholder payouts offer reasons for optimism. But with the stock having rallied sharply, is TM still worth buying? Let's dig deeper.
Toyota Motor Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Toyota Motor Corporation Quote

The decline in net income does not fully capture the improvement in Toyota's operations. The decline came from foreign-exchange losses and higher finance costs, which together outweighed an improvement in operating profit. Operating income grew 34% during the quarter under review.

The automotive division, Toyota's core, saw revenues rise 8.2% to ¥11.96 trillion. Its operating profit jumped 53% to ¥878.2 billion, helped by favorable currency movements, pricing actions and lower expenses, though higher material costs took a bite. The smaller "All Other" businesses also did well, with revenues up 19.6% and operating profit up 51% to ¥47.3 billion.
Financial services was the soft spot. Revenues rose 14% to ¥1.36 trillion, but operating income fell 13.8% to ¥196.7 billion. It is a modest drag next to the strength in autos.

Gary Black: Tesla’s US EV Share Fell “From 80% in 2020 to 52% Today”
sum: - Gary Black says Tesla’s share of US electric-car sales fell from 80% in 2020 to 52% today, as models from Hyundai, Toyota and GM gained.
- Tesla’s revenue was $94.8 billion in 2025, below 2023’s $96.8 billion, and its operating margin fell to 4.6% from 16.8% in 2022.
- At 187x forward earnings, well above its five-year average of 108x, Tesla’s price depends on FSD and autonomy far more than on car sales.
- Bulls point to paid FSD on more than 75% of new North American deliveries, but the bigger test is Robotaxi, which Elon Musk expects to move Tesla’s finances around the second quarter of 2027.
Tesla (TSLA) stock had a strong week. On October 31, The Future Fund’s Gary Black spent part of his Saturday arguing that the car business underneath it keeps losing ground.

Egypt Raises Over $650m In IPO Of State-Owned Bank
sum: Egypt on Monday raised more than $650 million in its initial public offering of the state-owned Banque du Caire, marking one of the biggest asset sales in years as international lenders push a privatisation drive.
The offering comes as Egypt advances reforms under an International Monetary Fund programme aimed at boosting private sector participation and reducing the state’s role in the economy.
The government has previously said it plans to sell stakes in over 30 state-owned companies under commitments linked to its IMF support programme.
The bank’s majority shareholder, Banque Misr, sold 6.86 billion shares, representing 45 percent of Banque du Caire, at 5.30 Egyptian pounds per share, according to the final offer announcement.
The sale raised about 36.37 billion pounds ($658 million) and valued the lender at around 80.83 billion pounds ($1.46 billion).
In June, authorities granted preliminary listings to four state-owned companies ahead of planned stock market offerings by May 2027.

Prime Minister Moustafa Madbouly said Monday’s listing came despite regional tensions and underscored the government’s commitment to “continuing its programme of state asset offerings, aiming to unlock greater value from public assets”.

Petrol Cars Lose No.1 Spot in India – CNG, Hybrid & EVs Together Take 42% Share
sum: India’s passenger-vehicle market has crossed an important milestone. For the first time, alternative-fuel passenger vehicles collectively outsold petrol-powered cars in a single month.
According to FADA’s August 2026 retail data, CNG/LPG, hybrids and EVs together accounted for 41.95% of passenger-vehicle registrations, marginally ahead of petrol/ethanol at 40.85%.
This is significant because India’s transition away from conventional petrol cars is not being driven by EVs alone. Instead, CNG, hybrids and electric cars are all contributing to the shift.
A year earlier, petrol/ethanol still accounted for 46.89% of passenger-vehicle retail, while CNG/LPG stood at 21.47%, hybrids at 8.13% and EVs at 5.38%.
That means petrol has lost roughly 6 percentage points of share in one year, while all three major alternative-powertrain categories have strengthened.
CNG/LPG remains by far the largest alternative-fuel category, accounting for 25.28% of passenger-vehicle sales in August.
That means roughly one in four cars registered in India now runs on CNG/LPG.

Honda officially reveals new CB1000F in three colour options
sum: After revealing the CB1000F as a concept during the prestigious Suzuka 8 Hour race in August, Honda has now revealed the finished product.
The new model arrives in three equally classy colourways, as well as sharing many similarities to the recently launched CB1000 Hornet.

According to Honda, the three paint schemes are called Wolf Silver Metallic with Blue Stripe, Wolf Silver Metallic with Grey Stripe and Graphite Black. The new model is expected to arrive in UK dealers in early 2026.

Now onto the bike itself, as the CB1000F is the latest model in what is a 65-year history for the CB family. Delving back into the archives, the new model specifically harps back to the 1980s, taking after the CB750F in its appearance.
That bike is one that racing fans from that era might remember well, as it powered American rider Freddie Spencer’s AMA Championship campaigns.

As I mentioned above, the CB1000 Hornet is an important bike to think of when looking at the new CB1000F, and that’s because the two bikes share many core components, although the latter has had its power output adjusted and moved down the rev range to offer a more relaxed riding experience.

Honda says it has been “developed under the conceptual target of creating the ‘Best Balanced Roadster’. The CB1000F handles like a middleweight but with big bike feel. And, with the ‘80s now proving such an influential decade in clothing, music, style, and more, the CB1000F is very much a bike ready for today.”

Japan's Honda reports robust results after its first ever annual loss
sum: TOKYO (AP) — Honda's profit for the fiscal first quarter more than doubled from a year ago, as the Japanese automaker continues to tackle a turnaround from the first full year loss in its history.
Tokyo-based Honda Motor Co. said Wednesday its April-June profit totaled 456.9 billion yen ($2.9 billion), up from 196.6 billion yen for the same period a year ago.
Quarterly sales rose 13.5% to 6.06 trillion yen ($38 billion), as vehicles sold well in the U.S. and India, according to the maker of the Accord sedan, Fit subcompact and Super Cub motorcycle.

Honda previously recorded a 423.9 billion yen ($2.7 billion) loss for the fiscal year ended in March, acknowledging heavy costs for its electric-vehicle plans, which didn't measure up to the original ambitions, partly because of U.S. President Donald Trump's policies.
Analysts say many consumers weren't ready to go electric. Honda has abandoned many of its plans for EV models.

The Trump administration has pulled back on incentive programs for EVs and withheld money to states wanting to add more EV charging stations, even as gas prices have soared over the war in Iran. Trump's tariffs on imported autos and auto parts, lowered to 15% from the initial 25%, also worked to dent Honda's profitability.
For the latest quarter, Honda's motorcycle operations were highly lucrative with sales going strong in Brazil and India. Car sales grew in Japan and the U.S., while struggling in China.

Disabled motorcyclist continues remarkable two-wheel journey at 75 years of age
sum: Max Jones, a long-time motorcyclist from Pembrokeshire, Wales, is continuing to ride bikes despite suffering from severe arthritis at the age of 75, and he does so by riding a Honda Gold Wing trike that features an attached trailer for his wheelchair.
Jones is a former police officer who has been riding motorcycles since the 1970s, and has completed trips to Ireland, Scotland and throughout Europe.

But due to his arthritis, Jones has had to change the way he goes riding, which includes transitioning from two wheels to three. When he’s not riding to his destinations, Jones also relies on the use of his four-wheel WHILL C2 powerchair, which is mounted inside his trailer for any trip he takes aboard his Gold Wing trike.

Jones served the police force for 27 years as a Constable, and later as a Sergeant. His roles were occupied across various areas of South Wales, while the 75-year-old also spent two years as a Law Instructor at the Welsh Police Training Centre.
Speaking about his journey to this point, along with the need to find a wheelchair that could support his current wishes to continuing riding, Jones said:

"If you start looking for a manual wheelchair when you are tall and 17 stone like me, you have a problem finding anything that will fit. And my wife was going to have to push me around which wouldn't be fair. You need something that will self-propel. I tried loads and, in the end, I believe the powered WHILL range is the best.

“You can't beat it; nothing compares to it. So comfortable. My grandad used to say: 'There's nothing more expensive than buying cheap'. It's an old saying but true and the WHILL has proven its worth many times over. In fact, it's been that good, Max has now invested in a second WHILL, the new folding C Lite for car, bus and train journeys.

Honda Rebel 300 & Rebel 500 Previewed for India: Honda’s Mid-Size Cruiser Dreams Are Finally Taking Shape
sum: Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India (HMSI) has finally given Indian cruiser enthusiasts something to look forward to. As part of its biggest-ever two-wheeler showcase featuring 10 new products, Honda displayed the Rebel 300 alongside the locally manufactured Rebel 500, signalling a renewed focus on India's fast-growing premium motorcycle segment. The Rebel twins were among the biggest crowd-pullers at the event, hinting that Honda is serious about challenging Royal Enfield, Kawasaki and other players in the middleweight cruiser space.
The Honda Rebel name has enjoyed a cult following internationally for years. While Indian enthusiasts have repeatedly demanded the motorcycle, Honda remained cautious about introducing it here.

That is now changing. The Rebel lineup is expected to become a key pillar of Honda's premium BigWing portfolio, offering an easy-to-ride cruiser with Japanese reliability and modern engineering rather than chasing traditional heavyweight cruiser styling.
The Rebel 300 has been designed as an approachable urban cruiser with a low-slung stance and minimalist bobber-inspired styling.
The motorcycle shares its engine platform with Honda's CB300 series, meaning maintenance costs and reliability should remain attractive for Indian buyers.

Honda previously sold the Rebel 500 in India as a Completely Built Unit (CBU), making it relatively expensive and limiting its reach. This time, the company has confirmed that the motorcycle will be manufactured locally, allowing for significantly better pricing and wider availability.
Unlike traditional chrome-heavy cruisers, the Rebel series adopts a clean, contemporary bobber look.

Honda delays takeover of Astemo
sum: Honda Motor has announced that it has delayed plans to make local automotive systems manufacturer Astemo Ltd a consolidated subsidiary. The Japanese automaker confirmed that it now expects to complete the acquisition of a majority stake in Astemo by the end of 2026, instead of by the end of the second quarter as it had originally announced in December 2025.

Honda currently holds a 40% stake in Astemo, with Japanese multinational company Hitachi Ltd also holding a 40% stake and JIC Capital (Japanese Investment Corporation) the holding the remaining 20%. Honda has agreed to acquire an additional 21% stake in Astemo from Hitachi, which would lift its holding in the company to 61%.

Astemo produces a wide range of automotive systems, including hardware and software for chassis and powertrain systems, as well as autonomous driving/advanced driver assistance (ADAS) systems, and is central to Honda's plans to develop and produce software-defined vehicles (SDVs) and improve its competitiveness.

Honda said in a statement: "In the face of the rapid and intense changes in the automotive business environment, it is essential for Honda, as a parent company, to lead the transformation of Astemo so that Astemo can pursue the establishment of a business structure that enables high-speed, high-efficiency development of AI and software technologies, which will become increasingly necessary in the era of SDVs. Based on this belief, Honda, Hitachi and JIC Capital agreed in December 2025, that Honda will acquire additional shares of Astemo, equivalent to 21% of all outstanding shares, from Hitachi, thereby changing the shareholding structure to 61% Honda, 19% Hitachi, and 20% JIC Capital.

Honda confirmed that since the initial announcement, it has been working to obtain the necessary clearances and approvals, but that delays in the approval process have resulted in the transaction now expected to be completed by the end of the third quarter of the current fiscal year (FY2026), which ends in March 2027.
"Honda delays takeover of Astemo" was originally created and published by Just Auto, a GlobalData owned brand.

TVS Motor vrooms past Hero, Honda to take top slot in 2-wheeler sales
sum: TVS Motor became India's top two-wheeler maker by total June sales, surpassing Hero MotoCorp and Honda on the back of strong domestic demand and exports

Tamil Nadu-based TVS Motor Company (TVSM), a part of the TVS Venu group, has become India's largest two-wheeler (2W) manufacturer by total sales volume, combining domestic and international business, for the month of June 2026. The company is already the market leader in the electric two-wheeler (e2W) segment.

The company sold 5.65 lakh units globally, taking the top spot ahead of long-standing leaders Hero MotoCorp, which sold 5.41 lakh units, and Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India, which sold 5.28 lakh units. Though the company had achieved a similar feat in the month of December 2025, it is generally a lean month for 2W-makers.

"This is the first time that we have become clear market leaders. Though a similar feat was achieved in December 2025, it is a post-season month where all players reduce their stocks. Even during Covid, TVS had outsmarted Hero and Honda, but that was also not a period which can be seen as normal," said a industry source.

During the month under review, TVS led Hero by 24,000 units and Honda by 37,000 units in total combined volume. Figures are company-reported wholesale dispatch numbers for June 2026. Total volume reflects combined India domestic dispatches and international business (export) dispatches.

Exports were the decisive factor in the company's performance. TVS's international business volume of 1.54 lakh units was 2.9 times the combined export volume of Hero and Honda. "The export volume reflects TVS's deepening presence across international markets, including Africa, Latin America, Asean, and West Asia, positioning it as an increasingly globally diversified two-wheeler manufacturer," said the source.

The result builds on a sustained multi-quarter trend, with TVS posting the fastest volume growth among major OEMs (original equipment manufacturers) through FY26, and steadily narrowing the gap with Hero and Honda, the source added. TVS grew by 47 per cent, far higher than Hero, Honda, and Bajaj during the month.

items.t: Honda CEO says Nissan tie-up is near; brands could share ECUs
sum: Back in February 2025, Nissan and Honda ended merger talks after the two companies couldn't come to a mutual agreement. With it, the hopes of seeing Nissan and Honda become the world's fourth-largest automaker became naught.

Despite the merger not happening, it seems both Honda and Nissan did not abandon possible tie-ups entirely. This comes after Honda Motor Corporation CEO Toshihiro Mibe shared that both brands are close to entering a partnership.

During the recent Honda shareholders' meeting, Mibe apologized to stakeholders after the company posted its first-ever annual loss in years. Combined with the brand turning away from their bold EV strategy, some questioned whether Mibe was making the right decisions. However, the CEO quelled fears by stating that they are working with Nissan for a partnership, with some aspect possibly close to an official announcement.

According to a report by Nikkei Asia, Honda, Nissan, and Mitsubishi could share common ECUs across a range of models, which includes hybrids and EVs. The shared ECUs could reach the market sometime in 2029 or 2030, as there are still questions about the development funding and other important aspects of the shared ECU between the brands. However, an agreement between the brands is expected to happen within weeks.

What could stop the deal between the two brands? Well, Nissan is part of the Renault Nissan Mitsubishi Alliance, and Renault still has a 15% voting stake in Nissan. Since Nissan is a publicly traded company, it will need shareholder consent to enter into any deal or partnership with another entity outside the Alliance.

With Honda and Nissan both in precarious financial situations, it seems both brands cannot afford not to have some sort of partnership. The only question now is, will the two brands actually come to an agreement, and will Renault actually let Nissan have a deal with Honda?
